title: Why Pakistan Tested an Extended Range Version of the Fatah-IV
author: Usman Haider
text:
In this still from a video posted by Pakistan’s nter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Pakistan test-launches the Fatah-IV ER variant on Oct. 6, 2026.
Credit: Screenshot from ISPR video
On October 6, Pakistan tested an extended range (ER) version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile. This was the third launch of the Fatah-IV missile system, the last having been conducted in May 2026. The latest test is unique compared to the first two, because this time the missile had a reported range of more than 750 kilometers. The Fatah-IV is a byproduct of the 2025 India-Pakistan clashes. The missile was first unveiled publicly during Pakistan’s Independence Day event on August 14, 2025. It features terrain-hugging flight capability intended to reduce radar detection, has a maximum speed of Mach 0.7, and carries a 330 kilogram blast-fragmentation explosive warhead. [...]
